entries.test: Reported annual losses and financial statements showing whether either company's profitability depends on accounting or financing adjustments rather than operating earnings.
entries.note: He mocks the prediction of dominance but asserts the losses and profitability limitation.
The proposition concerns NVIDIA's intention, rather than the observable revenue effects of its investments.
The source says trillions, not a single trillion-dollar bailout. It asserts a risk of destabilization, not a firm outcome.

entries.test: Public investment records, regulatory histories and media coverage establishing whether regulatory gaps and failures of media accountability materially drove speculative AI investment.
entries.note: This is a causal assertion that can be assessed using public evidence, even if attribution is difficult.
The sweeping description of every bit of hype as rebranding is polemical exaggeration.

entries.test: Anthropic's disclosures and contemporaneous reporting showing whether the $65 billion run rate had a defined calculation and whether coverage scrutinized it.
Anthropic's reported Q2 2026 revenue and public AI-company disclosures of actual revenue and underlying costs.
entries.note: The preceding discussion makes Anthropic the contextual referent for $11.6 billion.
The source says further spending buys a chance at revenue below Duolingo's; the normalization turns that into a firm revenue outcome. The current-loss component is separately checkable.
Calling a valuation irrational is an evaluative judgment without a specified valuation standard.
The valuations are checkable separately; describing the business models as questionable is evaluative.

entries.test: Investment timelines, investor statements and reporting showing whether VC and hyperscaler commitments prompted further investment by serving as evidence of commercial viability.
entries.note: The plain reading is a herd-investment mechanism, not a literal claim about every person's private beliefs.

entries.test: Operating AI data centers' permanent employment figures and public economic-impact records showing jobs, output and local benefits relative to their costs.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies the AI-data-center scope.

entries.test: Employment data for new AI industries and model-wrapper companies showing their workforce size relative to the broader labor market.
entries.note: The claim has a plain employment-scale reading despite the loose threshold.

entries.test: Power plans, permits and emissions records for the AI data centers Zitron has publicly discussed showing how commonly they use behind-the-meter gas turbines and their environmental effects.
entries.note: His personal sample limits the scope; this is not a claim about every AI data center.
Whether an explanation is compelling is a judgment, not a claim that no explanation exists.

entries.test: AI-service sales, usage and compute purchases attributable to customers other than OpenAI and Anthropic showing the scale of remaining demand.
NVIDIA's customer counts and quarterly receivables-concentration disclosures showing whether its customer base shrank and concentration increased.
entries.note: The adjacent sentences support the added receivables detail. Concentration alone would not establish declining customer numbers.

entries.test: NVIDIA's customer exposures, payment terms and major customers' financing records showing whether collections and sales rely on continued fundraising and data-center investment.
entries.note: This asserts a financial dependency rather than merely reporting a revenue figure.

entries.test: Google, Amazon and Microsoft's revenue from OpenAI and Anthropic over the three years following publication, compared with their total AI revenue and associated capital spending.
entries.note: The projected revenue amount and share are future outcomes, despite the present-tense framing of spending.

entries.test: Investor questions, earnings-call transcripts and market commentary immediately following any of the three companies stopping AI capital spending.
entries.note: The concrete predicted response is investor scrutiny if spending stops.

entries.test: Meta's product offerings and revenue disclosures showing whether it operates a substantive revenue-generating AI business.
entries.note: In context, an AI business means a commercial revenue source, not merely AI research or internal use.

entries.test: Publicly available financial statements and cost analyses establishing whether AI services or AI GPU rental businesses earn profits after relevant costs.
entries.note: The claim concerns the state of available evidence, not a firm prediction that profitability is impossible.
The central characterization is a judgment of worth supported by a sweeping critique of market beliefs.

entries.test: Evidence after the AI bubble's collapse showing whether surviving infrastructure, technologies or businesses provide continuing economic value.
entries.note: The normalization adds 'lasting' and resolves an ambiguous rejection of status-quo slogans into a specific post-bubble forecast.
The normalization removes 'to me' and changes 'not tremendously impressive' into 'not impressively.' The product-development component could be checked separately.
He judges whether useful automations justify the investment without specifying a financial-return test.

entries.test: Public model-behavior evaluations and controlled productivity studies measuring flattery, unsupported capability promises and perceived versus actual useful output.
entries.note: The normalization drops the universal flattery wording and turns a capability to create apparent productivity into a general assertion that LLMs do so.
'Scale of importance' supplies no shared outcome measure for assigning exclusive causation.
The normalization omits 'almost entirely' from the characterization of the industry's focus. Whether investment 'makes sense' is an evaluative judgment here.

entries.test: Public procurement records, customer commitments and financial-capacity evidence showing whether Lambda had other willing or capable customers for a comparable deal and sufficient diverse demand.
entries.note: The source says no one else was 'willing or capable'; the normalization asserts inability alone.

entries.test: Lease disclosures, credit assessments and reporting on the transaction showing whether NVIDIA assumed the lease because of Anthropic's financial instability.
entries.note: The words 'such ... that' assert a causal link.

entries.test: OpenAI and Anthropic's available funds, operating cash flows, financing commitments and compute-payment obligations showing whether they can cover the contracted costs.
Construction and commissioning records showing whether the Anthropic–Lambda data center becomes operational within the next two years after publication.
entries.note: 'For years' supplies a multi-year lower bound. 'If it ever does' does not weaken the firm near-term noncompletion claim.
Immediate revenue recognition is explicitly qualified by 'likely.' The separate construction-delay claim is firm.

entries.test: NVIDIA's customer revenue exposures and hyperscaler compute commitments showing the extent to which growth relies on large-company spending backed by OpenAI and Anthropic's projected compute purchases.
entries.note: The normalization drops 'entirely' from NVIDIA's dependency and strengthens 'largely based on' into 'hinges on.'

entries.test: Public financial statements and segment results showing whether any AI business outside the stated exceptions earns a profit from AI.
entries.note: The source names Jensen Huang personally; substituting NVIDIA changes the stated exception.

entries.test: Revenue, cost savings and productivity evidence from AI GPU uses outside OpenAI and Anthropic rentals, together with publicly documented prospective uses.
entries.note: The future-facing clause assesses current evidence for improvement rather than predicting that improvement cannot occur.

entries.test: Financing records, valuations, underlying cash flows and media coverage showing whether hyperscaler and NVIDIA capital and promotional reporting drove speculative AI investment and financial fragility.
Public polling, commentary and bailout demands after the AI bubble ends showing widespread questions about its causes and support for rescuing affected AI companies.
Technical evidence about LLM training and generation, product marketing and public behavioral evaluations showing how models use past data and respond to users.
entries.note: Outputs 'based on a summary' are not necessarily outputs that summarize past data. Coddling also does not necessarily mean flattery.
The normalization omits the claimed end of massive venture-capital returns. Neither 'end of hypergrowth' nor 'misallocated' has a shared threshold or horizon here.

entries.test: National productivity statistics and public empirical studies available at publication identifying any aggregate productivity gains attributable to AI.
entries.note: 'Does not appear' frames the current evidentiary picture rather than assigning a probability to a future outcome.
